stimulus.text:
President Woodrow Wilson, Proclamation of Neutrality, August 4, 1914 (verbatim excerpts):

"Whereas the laws and treaties of the United States, without interfering with the free expression of opinion and sympathy, or with the commercial manufacture or sale of arms or munitions of war, nevertheless impose upon all persons who may be within their territory and jurisdiction the duty of an impartial neutrality during the existence of the contest; . . . Now, Therefore, I, Woodrow Wilson, President of the United States of America, in order to preserve the neutrality of the United States . . . do hereby declare and proclaim . . . That the statutes and the treaties of the United States and the law of nations alike require that no person, within the territory and jurisdiction of the United States, shall take part, directly or indirectly, in the said wars, but shall remain at peace with all of the said belligerents, and shall maintain a strict and impartial neutrality . . ."
stimulus.source_note: Verbatim excerpts from Woodrow Wilson, Proclamation of Neutrality, August 4, 1914 (public domain).

stem: The policy Wilson announces in the proclamation changed most directly when

options.text: Congress passed the Espionage Act in 1917
options.misconception: The Espionage Act came after the United States was already at war; it did not end neutrality.

options.text: the United States declared war on Germany in April 1917
the Senate rejected the Treaty of Versailles in 1919
options.misconception: The treaty fight came after the war ended; neutrality had already ended in 1917.

options.text: American troops landed in France in 1918
options.misconception: Troops landed because the United States was already at war; the landing did not change the policy.

rationales.A: The Espionage Act came after the United States was already at war. It did not end neutrality.
rationales.B: The declaration of war in April 1917 ended neutrality. A nation at war with Germany could no longer be strictly neutral toward it.
rationales.C: The treaty fight came after the war ended. Neutrality had already ended in 1917.
rationales.D: Troops landed because the United States was already at war. The landing did not change the policy.
rationales.general:
1. Name the policy: strict and impartial neutrality toward all the warring nations.
2. Ask what event ends neutrality. A declaration of war does; laws and troop movements follow it.
3. Put the events in order. The declaration came first, in April 1917.
Remember: a policy ends when the act that defines it is reversed, not when its effects arrive.
